characterList.description: Woman with medium-length blonde hair, wearing round tortoise shell glasses and a black top. She is sitting in a chair in a room with a whiteboard and some bookshelves.
characterList.name: Kate Darling

content_metadata.description: Kate Darling discusses the complex relationship between AI and human behavior, emphasizing AI's role in social development, especially for children. She uses anecdotes to illustrate both potential benefits and concerns, advocating for ethical AI development.

qAndA.answer: She is particularly interested in the potential impact of AI on the behavioral development of children, specifically how interacting with Siri and Alexa might affect their social skills and communication patterns.
qAndA.question: What specific aspect of human development is Kate Darling particularly concerned about regarding AI interaction?

qAndA.answer: She references the ELIZA chatbot, a program from the 1960s that mimicked a psychoanalyst by responding with questions. Despite its simplicity, people readily opened up to ELIZA and revealed personal information, demonstrating the power of even basic AI to elicit human responses.
qAndA.question: What historical example does Kate Darling use to illustrate that even simple AI systems can significantly influence human behavior?

qAndA.answer: She cites two contrasting anecdotes – one about an autistic boy whose communication skills improved through interaction with Siri and another about a parent who felt Alexa was negatively influencing their children's politeness and social behavior.
qAndA.question: What specific example does Kate Darling provide to demonstrate both the potential positive and negative effects of AI on children?

qAndA.answer: She argues that understanding and addressing this issue requires collaboration between technologists, policymakers, researchers from fields like psychology and sociology, and users themselves.
qAndA.question: Why does Kate Darling believe that studying the impact of AI on human behavior is an interdisciplinary problem?

qAndA.answer: She hopes that in the next few years, the focus will shift towards harnessing the positive potential of AI and establishing ethical frameworks and policies to ensure its responsible and beneficial use for society.
qAndA.question: What is Kate Darling's ultimate hope for the future of AI?

characterInteraction.description: Kate Darling is the only character and interacts directly with the audience through the camera.

scenes.contextualRelevance: Exploration of AI's role in social development and ethical implications.

narrativeProgression.description: Kate Darling discusses the increasing use of AI in supporting human activities.
She highlights the social interaction aspect of AI and the impact of treating it like a social actor.
She raises the question of AI's effect on human behavior, particularly in children.
She uses anecdotes about Siri and Alexa to illustrate both potential benefits and concerns.
She emphasizes the need for research and the involvement of experts from various disciplines.
She concludes by advocating for a focus on the positive effects of AI and the development of ethical structures for its use.

scenes.thematicElements: Impact of AI on human behavior, especially children; Ethical considerations in AI design and development; Role of interdisciplinary research; Need for responsible and ethical AI development and use.
scenes.title: Scene 1

trimmingSuggestions.description: The explanation of how the ELIZA chatbot worked could be slightly condensed to maintain momentum and focus on the key takeaway – its impact on user behavior.
The section listing the various disciplines involved in AI research could be streamlined to retain the core message – interdisciplinary collaboration is crucial – without slowing down the pace.

text_to_speech: You know increasingly we're using automated technology in ways that kind of support humans and what they're doing rather than just having algorithms work on their own because they're not smart enough to do that yet or deal with unexpected situations. So we're interacting more and more with these systems and so you need an interface that makes sense for a human to interact with. And so a lot of these systems have an interface that is personified and that will talk to you. The effect that I'm so interested in the psychological effect of us treating these systems like social actors is actually - we achieved that in the 60s. Like in the 60s we had this chatbot called Eliza that Joseph Weizenbaum made. It's a really famous example of a really simple chatbot all it did was answer everything with a question like a psychoanalyst would. So if you're like "oh, I don't like my mom" it would be like "why don't you like your mom." And people would just open up and tell it all sorts of things, even though it was very primitive and how it behaved. So it's useful that we will engage with these systems on a social level because it's engaging for people and you can get people to actually use the systems more. But I do wonder whether there's any effect on our behavior. On our long-term behavioral development. It really gets interesting when we start talking about kids. You have these systems like Siri, and Alexa that kids are interacting with and if these systems are simulating lifelike behavior or a real conversation then that could actually influence kids' behavioral development and the way that they start to converse with other people. There's some examples of this just anecdotally that we have so far like there was an article in New York Times a few years ago about this kid, this autistic boy who developed a relationship with Siri. And the mom was like "this is the best thing ever. Siri is infinitely patient will answer all of his questions. Also the voice recognition is so shitty that he had to learn to articulate his words really well and it's made him a better communicator with other people because of Siri." But then on the other hand you have stories like this one guy wrote an article a few months ago about how Alexa was turning his kids into assholes because she doesn't require any please or thank you or any of the standard politeness that you want your kids to learn in conversing with others. So you know I think it is an interesting question that the more we're able to simulate like a real conversation with these systems the more that might get muddled in our subconscious in some way. One of the things that I think is really necessary is that we need to study more what impact this can have on our behavior. So we definitely need to be studying these interactions and studying the effects of these interactions. It's a similar question to violent video games or pornography. These are questions that have come up again and again but i think that these systems bring them to a new more visceral level in our psychology. So we need more research and then depending on what the answer to that specific question is we might need to think about design and use and maybe even policy for regulating these agents. Part of the problem is also that this is such an interdisciplinary problem. All of the questions that are coming up are so interdisciplinary you need technologists you need policymakers you need users you need researchers who understand psychology, who understand technology who understand sociology like all of this is coming together. And you need people talking to each other. I would really like us to in the next few years to lean into the positive effects of the technology and develop structures the way that we have in other fields like medicine to ensure that we're using the technology and responsible ethical way.

youtube_description:
Kate Darling of both the MIT Media Lab and the Berkman Klein Center for Internet & Society at Harvard University considers how interacting with artificially intelligent human agents can impact human behavioral development. 

Find out more about this project at http://brk.mn/ai
youtube_title: Kate Darling: AI and Human Development
